meanings.meaning: A priest is someone who offers sacrifices to God and acts for people in things that have to do with God. At first, fathers did this for their own families. Later, God set apart the family of Aaron, from the tribe of Levi, to serve as the priests of Israel.
The Holy Spirit is God. The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are three distinct Persons who are one God. The Holy Spirit helps and strengthens God's people.
A being that has no body, such as an angel or a demon. Good spirits are angels who serve God. Bad spirits, also called unclean spirits, are demons.
The part of a person that is inside, the part that feels and lives, not the body. It can be a person's life, soul, or feelings, such as when someone feels weak or discouraged.

A serious agreement or promise between two sides. In the Bible, a covenant is often God's serious promise to people, like his promises to Noah and Abraham. People are sometimes asked to do their part, such as obeying him. The Hebrew word means "a cutting," because long ago people made an agreement by cutting animals in two and walking between the pieces, which showed the agreement was official.
A day of rest that God set apart for His people, usually the seventh day of the week. On it they stopped their work and kept the day special for God.
A special year of rest, every seventh year, when the Israelites let their land rest.
A person who writes songs about God or for worship. The name is especially used for David and the other writers of the songs in the book of Psalms.

To scatter something in small drops or bits, like water, blood, oil, or dust, so it lands on a person or thing. In the Bible, sprinkling is often done to make people or things clean or set apart for God.
To die or be destroyed, or to pass away and be lost completely. It can be used for people or animals dying, and also for things that fade away, wear out, or come to nothing.
Almighty means having all power, with no limit to how strong or mighty someone is. In the Bible it is a name for God, the One with all power.

A special piece of clothing worn by priests. It had a front part and a back part joined over the shoulders and tied at the waist with a belt. The high priest's ephod was fancier, with colorful embroidery, and his breastpiece was attached to it.
Something like the priest's ephod that was made and kept for worship, not worn by the high priest. Gideon made one in Ophrah, and people ended up worshiping it. Micah also had one in his shrine.

Leaven is something like yeast, or a lump of old dough that has soured and bubbled, that is mixed into new dough to make bread puff up and get light. It spreads quietly through all the dough. In the Bible it can also stand for something that spreads quietly, like bad teaching or sin, or like the kingdom of heaven growing. Leavened bread is bread made with leaven.

Impurity is anything that spoils or dirties something so it is no longer clean and pure. In the Bible it can mean wrongdoing, like sin and idol worship. It can also mean a condition under Israel's laws, like menstrual impurity, that was not a sin but kept a person from joining in worship until they were made clean.

Sorcery is the practice of magic, like using spells or trying to tell the future, sometimes with the supposed help of evil spirits. Sorcerers pretended they could predict events, heal sickness, or do miracles. The Bible warns that God judges people who practice it or trust in it.
A valuable gemstone with stripes or layers of different colors, like white and reddish bands. It was used in the high priest's clothing and was counted among the great treasures.
Sacrificing means offering something to God as an act of worship, usually an animal killed and burned on an altar. People did this to thank God, to ask for his favor, or to make up for their sins.
A blasphemer is someone who speaks about God in a disrespectful, insulting way. In Leviticus, the Hebrew words mean literally 'the one who cursed.'
A stick or piece of wood that is burning, or has been burning and is charred at the end. In the Bible it is sometimes a torch, and in Proverbs it can mean a flaming arrow or dart.
Stewardship is the job of a steward, someone trusted to manage something that belongs to another person. In these verses, the job is looking after and carrying out what God has given.
Someone who came from the family of a man named Ahoah. Several of David's brave warriors, like Eleazar, were called Ahohites because they were Ahoah's descendants.

Ethanim is the name of the seventh month on the old Hebrew calendar, which falls in about September and October. It was also the first month of the year for everyday life, and its name may mean the month of gifts. Later it was called Tisri.
